title: Chapter 1: Changes
draft: Chapter 1 - A War Without Sound (Draft 1, before revision).md
intro_md:
Written on 26 September 2026. This is every change made to `Chapter 1 - A War Without Sound.md` since the draft, each with a before, an after and a reason.

- **Revision 1** (changes 1–37) carried out the agreed decisions and craft fixes.
- **Revision 2** (changes 38–44) trimmed your own lines against principle 5: don't explain the meaning.
- **Revision 3** (changes 45–49) is the final check: small craft fixes from a last full read.

- The chapter as it was before is saved, unchanged, as `Drafts/Chapter 1 - A War Without Sound (Draft 1, before revision).md`. Any change you reject can go straight back from there.
- **Draft line** numbers refer to that saved copy. **Revised line** numbers refer to the chapter as it stands now.
- Nothing was changed that isn't listed here.
- Changes 6, 19, 20, 25, 27 and 37 were trimmed after your note on over-explaining. Each one shows the trimmed version.
glance: **Gerolt's failed laugh:** four times before (lines 103, 277, 417, 471). Now once, in your own line 103.
**"What do you remember before this morning?":** asked three times before, once now.
**"Leave your clothes alone":** three times before, twice now.
**"Almost heard":** 2 before, 1 after. The word he can't hear is still mentioned twice in the vision itself.
summary_md:
## What each decision became

**The six decisions you agreed**

1. **The belief that stays wrong** is the running figure: change {tag:belief}.
2. **Gerolt expects people by morning:** change {tag:deadline}.
3. **Gerolt knows about the scout agreement:** change {tag:scouts}.
4. **The sword, planted with one glance:** change {tag:sword}.
5. **"The boy", with one age cue:** change {tag:age}.
6. **First name only:** nothing to change. The chapter already calls him just "Gerolt".

**Earlier decisions**

- **The flame (locked):** changes {tag:flame}.
- **"Empty" is spoken,** and his fear turns to what the world does to people with no magic: changes {tag:fear}.
- **Gerolt reacts to the dead elves:** change {tag:elves}.
- **Gerolt's peace, and the boy ending it:** changes {tag:peace}.
- **Gerolt's damage, shown through what he does:** changes {tag:damage}, plus the sword glance ({tag:sword}) and his knowing the scouts ({tag:scouts}). The candle burn and the practised way he smothers the fire were already there.
- **The thesis passages (Principle 3):** changes {tag:thesis}.

**Craft fixes from the first review**

- The repeated question: changes {tag:repeat-q}. The clothes warnings: changes {tag:clothes}. The failed laughs: changes {tag:laugh}.
- Exact repeats of "nothing": changes {tag:nothing}. "Almost heard": change {tag:almost}. The over-polished line: change {tag:polish}.
- Staging: changes {tag:staging}. Spelling: changes {tag:spelling}. Point of view: change {tag:pov}. The duplicate wound line: change {tag:dup}. Time of day: change {tag:time}. The last line: change {tag:last}.
- Found while revising: the unattributed "Wena?" (change {tag:wena}).

## Left alone on purpose

- **Your opening (draft lines 3–115).** Only staging, spelling and one cut (changes 1–5). THOOM, the Light searching him, Gerolt checking the field "the way a man checks a door", and your line 103 laugh are all untouched.
- **Gerolt's numbers.** "Fifty winters on this land", "thirty years of traders" and "sixty years" put him near seventy. His age is still open in `Decisions.md`, so they stay until you decide.
- **The heading.** The old Rewrites files used a different format, but they no longer set the standard. Yours stands.
- **Everything the Revision Notes list under "keep":** the circle and the white flower, the left hand and the wrist, the vision, the choice ("He wanted answers. He chose silence."), the dismount with no sound and the four knocks.
- **"*Was I here with them?*"** stays a question he can't answer.

sections.Revision 2: Revision 2: your own lines, against principle 5

changes.title: Spelling
changes.before: Light—though his eyes were still shut, still crusted with mud. It came from nowhere outside him and swallowed everything regardless. For one impossible moment there was no mud beneath him, no sky above, no up or down at all. Only the sense of being pulled thin toward somewhere he would never reach.
changes.after: Light—though his eyes were still shut, still crusted with mud. It came from nowhere outside him and swallowed everything regardless. For one impossible moment there was no mud beneath him, no sky above, no up or down at all. Only the sense of being pulled thin towards somewhere he would never reach.
changes.why: "toward" becomes "towards". The house style uses British spelling.

changes.title: He can't see the sun yet
changes.before: The sun stood directly overhead. Inches from his face, a dead man's hand jutted out of the mud, fingers still curled around a spear shaft snapped off halfway up its length.
changes.after: Inches from his face, a dead man's hand jutted out of the mud, fingers still curled around a spear shaft snapped off halfway up its length.
changes.why: He's lying face-down with his cheek in the mud, so he can't see the sun overhead. The sentence isn't lost: it moves to change 4, the moment he's rolled onto his back.

changes.title: The body across his ribs
changes.before: Heavy hands closed on his shoulders.
changes.after: The cold weight across his ribs was heaved aside. Heavy hands closed on his shoulders.
changes.why: Line 9 puts "something heavy lying across his ribs" on him, and nothing ever moved it. Now it's heaved off before he's rolled over. "Cold" answers your "none of the warmth a body should have".

changes.title: The sun, and the first thesis line
changes.before: He shut his eyes against the glare and breathed in ragged pulls. Beneath the pain, one fact surfaced and stayed there: he was alive. He understood the word completely. He couldn't remember the life it was meant to describe.
changes.after: The sun stood directly overhead. He shut his eyes against it and breathed in ragged pulls. Beneath the pain, one fact surfaced and stayed there: he was alive.
changes.why: The sun sentence lands where he can finally see it. The last two sentences explained the memory rule instead of living it (Principle 3). Your own line 13, "He didn't know what his own voice sounded like", already lives the same rule, and better.
changes.call: These two sentences are your own writing. If you want to keep them, say so and they go back.

changes.title: Spelling
changes.before: He looked toward the horizon, and forgot to breathe.
changes.after: He looked towards the horizon, and forgot to breathe.
changes.why: British spelling again.

changes.title: The machines
changes.before: The boy knew carts and wheels. He knew what hammers, fire and ordinary hands could shape in a forge. None of that explained these things, yet the word *machine* came to him before he could ask for it. He could not have said how they worked. He knew what they had been built to do.
changes.after: *Machines.* The word came to him before he could ask for it. He could not have said how they worked. Looking at that blackened opening, he knew what they had been built to do.
changes.why: Principle 3. The old passage set out what he knows (carts, forges) the way a rulebook would. Now the word simply arrives, as 『Magic』 does later in the same scene. His word "machines" against Gerolt's "silver devils" at the window stays as a small clue. *Trimmed after your note on over-explaining: "and he didn't like how easily it came" is gone.*

changes.title: The wound line said twice
changes.before: Blood covered the boy's clothes. He found no wound beneath it.
changes.after: He looked down at the blood stiffening on his clothes.
changes.why: "He found no wound" repeated Gerolt's "Not a mark on you" from line 103, a leftover from joining two drafts. The blood on his own clothes still leads straight into "*Was I here with them?*"

changes.title: The walk back
changes.before: He talked through the whole walk back, low and constant, the way a man talks when he needs to keep his own hands steady.
changes.after: He kept talking, low and constant, the way a man talks when he needs to keep his own hands steady.
changes.why: Point of view. The boy is passing out, so he can't know Gerolt talked "the whole walk back". He can hear that Gerolt keeps talking.

changes.title: One of everything
changes.before:
The boy knew what the table was for. He understood why the pots hung beside the hearth and why the shutters had been closed against the night. He knew the purpose of everything he saw.

He could not remember where he had learned any of it.
changes.after: One bowl sat on the counter. One coat hung by the door. There was one bed, and he was lying in it.
changes.why: Two things at once. This was a thesis passage (Principle 3). And Gerolt's peace wasn't on the page: a man who lives alone by choice owns one of everything, and the stranger is in his only bed. It also agrees with the stew later, where Gerolt takes "a wooden bowl from the counter" and hands it over.
changes.call: This is a new detail about how Gerolt lives.

changes.title: Where Gerolt sits
changes.before: The old man from the battlefield sat on a low stool beside the hearth. A dented metal mug rested between his hands, and his shoulders sagged as he stared into the fire.
changes.after: The old man from the battlefield sat on a low stool beside the hearth. He had set it where he could see both the bed and the door. A dented metal mug rested between his hands, and his shoulders sagged as he stared into the fire.
changes.why: Gerolt's damage, shown through what he does: an old soldier still sits facing the door. It's the first of several small signs (see the list of decisions at the top).
changes.call: This is a new behaviour for Gerolt.

changes.title: Time of day
changes.before: "Easy now. You've been senseless since morning. If you mean to sit up, do it slowly. I'm too old to catch you twice in one day."
changes.after: "Easy now. You've been senseless since midday. If you mean to sit up, do it slowly. I'm too old to catch you twice in one day."
changes.why: He was found at noon (the sun overhead, the frost "beneath the midday sun"), so "since morning" was wrong.

changes.title: The second failed laugh
changes.before: A small laugh escaped him, though it didn't reach far.
changes.after: He pressed a fist into the small of his back to prove it.
changes.why: This was the second of four places where Gerolt's laugh fails (lines 103, 277, 417, 471). Your own at line 103 stays. Here his humour becomes something he does: his back really does hurt from carrying the boy.

changes.title: The second failed laugh (continued)
changes.before: Gerolt's laughter stopped.
changes.after: Gerolt forgot about his back.
changes.why: Goes with the change above. His attention leaves the joke the moment the boy says he's never heard of Mydea.

changes.title: The age cue
changes.before: "Leave the cloth alone before you unpick the poor thing entirely," Gerolt said. "We'll start simpler. What do people call you?"
changes.after: "Leave the cloth alone before you unpick the poor thing entirely," Gerolt said. "We'll start simpler. You've twenty winters on you, maybe. Somebody's been calling you something for every one of them. What is it?"
changes.why: Decision 5: keep "the boy", and restore one age cue so readers know he's a young man, not a child. It also sharpens the name question: twenty years of people calling him something, and none of it left.

changes.title: "Nothing came."
changes.before: Nothing came.
changes.why: It repeated your line 7, "Nothing came out." The paragraph before it ("Instead, he sat there with his lips parted while Gerolt waited") already carries the beat.

changes.title: The same question, second time
changes.before:
"I know what those things are. I can picture them when you say the words." The boy gripped the blanket harder. "None of them feel familiar."

"Nothing before this morning?"

"There has to be something." The boy heard his voice rising and could not stop it. "I can't have *nothing*."
changes.after: "I know what those things are. I can picture them when you say the words." The boy gripped the blanket harder. "None of them feel familiar. There has to be something." He heard his voice rising and could not stop it. "I can't have *nothing*."
changes.why: "Nothing before this morning?" was the second of three times Gerolt asks what he remembers before waking (lines 287, 343, 455). Now the panic rises out of the boy's own answer instead of the same question again.

changes.title: The second clothes warning
changes.before:
"Easy. You're shaking badly enough without tearing your clothes to pieces on top of it."

The boy barely heard him. His hands returned to his collar, then his cuffs, then every strip of stitching he could reach.
changes.after: His hands returned to his collar, then his cuffs, then every strip of stitching he could reach.
changes.why: The second of three times Gerolt tells him to leave his clothes alone (lines 321, 347, 355). Two remain: the joke and the wrist catch.

changes.title: The third clothes warning
changes.before: "Wait." Gerolt caught his wrist as his nail found another stitch. "Leave the coat alone. There's one more thing worth trying before you pull it apart. What's your 『Affinity』?"
changes.after: "Wait." Gerolt caught his wrist as his nail found another stitch. "There's one more thing worth trying before you pull it apart. What's your 『Affinity』?"
changes.why: "Leave the coat alone" repeated "Leave the cloth alone". Catching his wrist does the work.

changes.title: The flame
changes.before:
"So it isn't something I learned," he said slowly. "Not like knowing what a spoon is for without remembering who put one in my hand. It's more like my height or the colour of my eyes. Something that's there whether I remember it or not."

"Aye. Close enough."

"Then how could I lose it?" His voice caught somewhere in the question, and he had to push through it. "How could there be nothing?"

"There isn't supposed to be." Gerolt's mug sat forgotten between his hands. "That's my whole point."

"Then try telling me how to find it, instead of just telling me it's there."

"Close your eyes. Don't chase after it—that only scares it off. Sit still and feel for whichever one already belongs to you."

"That explains nothing."

"I know. Nobody's ever had to explain it to me before. It's just—there. The way a man doesn't need someone to point out he's got hands."
changes.after:
Gerolt read his face and gave up on explaining. He set the mug on the floor and held out one hand between them, palm up.

A flame opened in it.

It was no bigger than a candle's, and there was no wick beneath it, no oil, no wood. It leaned when Gerolt breathed, then straightened. Its light moved over the calluses on his palm.

The boy forgot the stitches and the blanket and the pounding in his skull.

『Magic』

The word rose from the same place as before, whole and certain. The boy kept it behind his teeth.

Gerolt closed his hand, and the flame went out between his fingers without smoke. When he opened it again and rested it on his knee, the skin of his palm had reddened, as if he'd held it too near the hearth. He didn't look at it.

"That's mine," he said. "Fire. Now close your eyes. Don't chase after it—that only scares it off. Sit still and feel for whichever one already belongs to you."
changes.why: The locked flame decision, following the outline you agreed. The talk about Affinity (the spoon, his height, "That explains nothing") goes, and the boy sees magic for the first time instead. He thinks 『Magic』 and doesn't say it; readers can see for themselves that it isn't Gerolt's word. His palm reddens: magic costs its user. The flicker is small and practised, so it doesn't break "no fire in a fight until his last stand". Gerolt's instruction survives word for word. *Trimmed after your note on over-explaining: "Fire needed something to burn. This one had only the man holding it." and "it wasn't the word Gerolt had used" are gone.*
changes.call: The reddened palm answers an open question in Decisions.md. It was step 4 of the outline you locked, so I've written it in; say no and it comes out (with the matching detail in change 25).

changes.title: Why he tries
changes.before: The boy closed his eyes anyway. Gerolt had carried him home, cleaned him and given him the bed. The least he could do was try.
changes.after: The boy closed his eyes.
changes.why: He used to close his eyes "anyway", answering the cut "That explains nothing", and then the narration gave his reason ("the least he could do was try"). After the flame, he needs no reason. *Trimmed after your note on over-explaining: the first version spelled out his hope instead.*

changes.title: What he finds inside
changes.before: That was all of it. Fire beside him. Wind beyond the shutters. Nothing inside him answered either.
changes.after: That was all of it. Fire beside him. Wind beyond the shutters. And inside him, a gap he could feel the edges of, the way a tongue keeps finding the place a tooth used to be.
changes.why: "Nothing answered" is on the watch-list. The flame decision says he recognises magic from outside and knows something is *missing* inside him. A gap with edges is missing; a blank would just be empty.
changes.decision_note: Rejected. You prefer the original: "I don't like over explaining meaning that make readers think beyond the obvious." The original line stays.

changes.title: Gerolt pulls back, then leans in
changes.before:
Gerolt's fingers tightened around the mug. One leg of the stool scraped across the floor as his weight shifted back, scarcely an inch, but the sound cut through the room. His gaze dropped to the boy's empty hands and then flicked towards the door.

For one breath, he looked at the boy the way he had looked at the violet sparks.

Then Gerolt set the mug on the floor, planted both boots and leaned towards him again.
changes.after:
Gerolt's hand closed over his knee. One leg of the stool scraped across the floor as his weight shifted back, scarcely an inch, but the sound cut through the room. His gaze dropped to the boy's empty hands and then flicked towards the door.

Then Gerolt planted both boots and leaned towards him again.
changes.why: The mug is already on the floor, so it can't be in his hand; the hand on his knee is the burned one. "The way he had looked at the violet sparks" made his fear an unease *of* the boy. The decision is that he fears *for* him. The glance at the door stays, and now points at who might come.

changes.title: What Gerolt said
changes.before: "You said I would know it." The words came faster now, and once they started he found he couldn't slow them back down. "You said I'd feel it before I could even put words to it. I don't feel fire. I don't feel water. I don't feel earth or wind or some fifth thing you haven't mentioned because you're hoping I won't need it. I feel a fire that isn't mine, and wind that isn't mine, and a headache that's at least probably my own, and that is the whole list, Gerolt. That is every single thing I have."
changes.after: "You said it already belongs to me." The words came faster now, and once they started he found he couldn't slow them back down. "You said I'd feel it. I don't feel fire. I don't feel water. I don't feel earth or wind or some fifth thing you haven't mentioned because you're hoping I won't need it. I feel a fire that isn't mine, and wind that isn't mine, and a headache that's at least probably my own, and that is the whole list, Gerolt. That is every single thing I have."
changes.why: With the talk cut, the boy's quote has to match what Gerolt actually said ("whichever one already belongs to you"). The rest of the speech is untouched. "A fire that isn't mine" now means two fires.

changes.title: Too polished
changes.before: "So either I'm doing this wrong," the boy said, quieter now that the anger had burned through as fast as it had come, "or there's actually nothing there. Tell me which. Because ever since I woke, I've been finding out I'm missing things one piece at a time, and I would rather hear it plainly than keep discovering it the way I discovered I don't have a name."
changes.after: "So either I'm doing this wrong," the boy said, quieter now that the anger had burned through as fast as it had come, "or there's actually nothing there. Tell me which. Ever since I woke, I've been finding out what's missing one piece at a time. I'd rather hear this one from you."
changes.why: "The way I discovered I don't have a name" is too neat for someone this frightened; the design bible says he shouldn't have polished explanations for himself. "I'd rather hear this one from you" keeps the request and shows he has started to trust Gerolt.

changes.title: "Empty"
changes.before: "I don't know which," he said finally. "That's the truth of it. I've seen men forget their wives. I've seen men forget the war. I've never seen one come up this empty." He rubbed both palms against his knees. "I keep hoping if I say the right thing, something in you will just—answer. Like calling a dog that's wandered off. Maybe it didn't hear you the first time."
changes.after:
"I don't know which," he said finally. "That's the truth of it. I've seen men forget their wives. I've seen men forget the war. I've seen Faint who couldn't warm a cup of water to save their lives, and even they had something that answered when they called." He rubbed both palms against his knees, one more carefully than the other. "You're not Faint. You're…"

He seemed to search for the word.

"Empty?"

When Gerolt spoke again, it was quieter, and not quite to the boy. "They test every child at ten. The ones who come up Faint get taken off their mothers, and they call it protection."

"What about someone with none?"

Gerolt's gaze had gone to the door, and it stayed there, as if someone might already be standing on the other side of it.

"I keep hoping if I say the right thing, something in you will just—answer," he said at last. "Like calling a dog that's wandered off. Maybe it didn't hear you the first time."
changes.why: Three decisions meet here. "Empty" is spoken, as a question, and as a word Gerolt has to invent (the old World Bible says no word exists for someone with no Affinity). His fear turns to what his world does to people with little or no magic, and he won't say what happens to someone with none: he looks at the door. Then his humour covers it, which is the Cid in him. *Trimmed after your note on over-explaining: "and not to like the one he found" and the boy turning the word over are gone, so "Empty?" stands on its own.*
changes.call: "Faint", the testing at ten and "they call it protection" are new on the page. They come from the old World Bible's class table and its "protective stewardship", so tell me if any of that has changed.
changes.decision_note: Kept. The old class lore is still true.

changes.title: The third failed laugh
changes.before: "Then you call again. Louder." Something almost like a smile crossed his face, though there wasn't much behind it. "I'm a farmer, not a scholar. Calling louder is the whole of my strategy."
changes.after: "Then you call again. Louder. I'm a farmer, not a scholar. Calling louder is the whole of my strategy."
changes.why: The third failed laugh, as a failed smile. He tells the joke straight, and the boy doesn't answer (see change 42).

changes.title: "Long enough"
changes.before: "Long enough." His jaw worked once. "And in all those years, I never saw men fight beside beastfolk."
changes.after: "Long enough. And in all those years, I never saw men fight beside beastfolk."
changes.why: "His jaw worked" is a watch-list gesture, and Gerolt's third jaw beat in the chapter. With no beat at all, the short answer does the holding back. *Trimmed after your note on over-explaining: "He didn't say how long" is gone.*

changes.title: The elves, and the deadline
changes.before: "So either I've been wrong about how the world works for sixty years, or something out there made it true just long enough to kill every one of them."
changes.after:
"And the pale ones?" the boy asked. "With the pointed ears?"

"Natharul." Gerolt said it low, as if the dark outside might carry it. "When one of theirs dies, they don't ask who did it. They ask where."

The boy thought of the pale faces among the dead. "Then they'll ask about here."

"Aye. And the nearest house with children in it is two fields over." He was still watching the dark where the field lay. "Come first light, somebody'll see the crows. By noon, somebody'll have sold what they saw, and there'll be men at my door asking what I found out there."
changes.why: Two decisions: Gerolt reacts to the dead elves, and he expects people by morning. His window speech named the banners, the armour, the machines and the beastfolk, and stopped short of the elves. Now the boy notices what he left out and asks, which is the boy's personality working. "They ask where" shows Natharul's collective punishment through Gerolt's fear instead of explaining it. The deadline is Mydea's informers: someone sees, someone sells. It's also the moment his peace visibly ends: "what I found out there" is the boy.
changes.call: The neighbours' house with children is new. They're unnamed, and nothing else about them is decided. One knock-on: because Gerolt now says "Natharul" out loud here, the name he swallows when the riders arrive ("His mouth started to shape a name") now reads as something more specific he recognises. That leaves a small question for Chapter 2. If you'd rather the swallowed name was simply "Natharul", this line would have to say "Elves" instead.
changes.decision_note: Kept: Gerolt names Natharul here, the name he swallows later is something more specific, and the neighbours' house stays.

changes.title: Who says "Wena?"
changes.before: "Wena?"
changes.why: An unattributed "Wena?" straight after "The boy looked down" reads as the boy speaking, and he can't know her name. Gerolt's next line introduces her anyway. This one wasn't on the original list; I found it while revising.

changes.title: The same question, third time
changes.before:
"Anything before you opened your eyes?"

"The first thing I remember is waking in that field."

Gerolt's shoulders lowered.
changes.after: Gerolt let go of the shutter.
changes.why: The third time he's asked what he remembers. The question just before it ("Anyone you heard speak, before I found you?") asks something new, so it stays, and with the deadline it now reads as pressure. "Gerolt's shoulders lowered" would have landed straight after "The boy lowered his eyes", so he lets go of the shutter instead.

changes.title: The fourth failed laugh
changes.before: An unsteady breath escaped Gerolt, almost becoming a laugh.
changes.why: The fourth failed laugh. The stew he's already getting up to fetch is his warmth.

changes.title: "Nothing else he could do"
changes.before: The boy obeyed because there was nothing else he could do. One shallow breath followed another until his chest finally loosened. Only then did Gerolt ease his grip.
changes.after: The boy obeyed. One shallow breath followed another until his chest finally loosened. Only then did Gerolt ease his grip.
changes.why: It repeated your line 31 word for word.

changes.title: "Almost heard"
changes.before: "I couldn't see their face." The boy caught at Gerolt's sleeve. "They were close enough that they should have reached me, but they kept running and never came any nearer. Their mouth kept moving. I almost heard—"
changes.after: "I couldn't see their face." The boy caught at Gerolt's sleeve. "They were close enough that they should have reached me, but they kept running and never came any nearer. Their mouth kept moving. They were saying something to me—"
changes.why: "Almost heard" was used three times before Chapter 2 pays it off. It stays at line 523 ("This time, he almost heard it"). Here he tells Gerolt the word was meant for him, which feeds what he decides a few lines later.

changes.title: The belief that stays wrong
changes.before: "How could I know?" His voice came out level and far too quiet. "I woke surrounded by bodies. Maybe they were trying to save me. Or maybe I was what they came to stop."
changes.after: "How could I know?" His voice came out level and far too quiet. "I woke surrounded by bodies. Every one of them was there to fight. Why would that one be any different?" The answer was out before he could hold it back. "I was what they came to stop."
changes.why: Decision 1. He reasons his way to it: everyone on that field was there to fight, so she must have been too. He's right about the army and wrong about her. The reader will learn she was running to reach him, and in Volume 3 he'll make the same mistake about the same person. Gerolt still doesn't correct him.

changes.title: The sword
changes.before: Gerolt was at the window before the boy could ask what was wrong. He pressed one eye to the gap in the shutters, and whatever he saw out there wiped the exhaustion from his face and left only fear behind.
changes.after: Gerolt glanced once at the floorboards beneath the table. Then he was at the window before the boy could ask what was wrong. He pressed one eye to the gap in the shutters, and whatever he saw out there wiped the exhaustion from his face and left only fear behind.
changes.why: Decision 4: plant the sword. One glance, no explanation. Chapter 2 pays it off (in the old Chapter 2, the sword is under a floorboard at the table). *Tightened in the final check: the first version said "Gerolt's gaze dropped", which is already used earlier.*

changes.title: Seen
changes.before: "Riding openly across Mydean fields…" His voice was barely there. "They shouldn't be here. Not ever."
changes.after: "They're letting themselves be seen." His voice was barely there. "They don't do that. Not ever."
changes.why: Decision 3: Natharul's scouts are always in Mydea and never seen, and Gerolt knows it. What shocks him is that they're showing themselves. The boy can't understand it; the reader gets the first hint of Gerolt's past. Your "Not ever" stays. It also answers the boy's "*They saw me*" a few lines earlier.

changes.title: The last line
changes.before:
The boy's breath stopped halfway in. A thought surfaced from the same empty place that had given him the word 『Magic』.

*Opening that door would be the last thing he ever did.*
changes.after:
The boy's breath stopped halfway in. A thought surfaced from the same empty place that had given him the word 『Magic』.

Opening that door would be the last thing either of them ever did.
changes.why: It was in italics but in the third person (italics are for direct thought), and "he" could be Gerolt or the boy. It's now plain narration, with "either of them". Your sentence before it already says the thought comes from the same place that gave him 『Magic』, so it reads as recognising magic, not as a sixth sense for danger (which Alaric's guardrails rule out). *Trimmed after your note on over-explaining: the two sentences explaining the silent footsteps are gone.*
changes.call: If you meant "he" to be one of them in particular, tell me which and I'll make it that one.
changes.decision_note: Kept: "either of them" is what you meant.

changes.title: "Interrupted"
changes.before: Neither man had reached the other. The battle had not ended so much as been *interrupted*.
changes.after: Neither man had reached the other.
changes.why: The second sentence told readers what the image means. The horse falling mid-stride and the two reaching hands already show it.

changes.title: "Appeared"
changes.before: Nothing had entered through the crop. The entire battlefield had appeared in its midst without bending a single stalk beyond it.
changes.after: Nothing had entered through the crop.
changes.why: The paragraph before it (no wheel ruts, no trail of broken wheat) and "Nothing had entered through the crop" already make the point. The second sentence drew the conclusion for the reader.

changes.title: The empty centre
changes.before: The boy stared at the empty centre. Some part of him insisted it should not have been empty.
changes.after: The boy stared at the empty centre.
changes.why: "*Someone was there.*" comes straight after and does the work.

changes.title: The name of a kingdom
changes.before: It was the name of an entire kingdom, and the boy had never heard it before. His fingers closed around the blanket as he waited for the name to stir something inside him. Nothing did.
changes.after: His fingers closed around the blanket as he waited for the name to stir something inside him. Nothing did.
changes.why: He says "I've never heard it before" himself two paragraphs later.

changes.title: Too tired to find it funny
changes.before: The boy didn't answer that. He was too tired to find it funny, and too frightened to let it comfort him, and he sat there with both feelings pressing on him at once until neither one won.
changes.after: The boy didn't answer that.
changes.why: The rest named his feelings. His silence after Gerolt's joke already shows them.

changes.title: Whose choice
changes.before: Calling out wouldn't be the boy's choice alone. It would make it for both of them.
changes.why: The paragraphs before it show Gerolt hiding in his own house, and "He wanted answers. He chose silence." carries the choice.

changes.title: Enough for the boy
changes.before: For now, that was enough for the boy too.
changes.why: "But he knew enough to be afraid." is the stronger place to stop.

changes.title: The same oath twice
changes.before: "Easy—by the Four, lad!"
changes.after: "Easy, lad!"
changes.why: Line 69 already has "Easy, lad—by the Four", and oaths are meant to be used sparingly. The chapter still has "By the Four" twice (lines 69 and 291) and "the Last Dark" twice.

changes.title: Looking down three times
changes.before: The boy looked down at the fabric. "I wish I could tell you. I keep looking for something in them—a mark, a colour, anything that might explain who made them or why I was wearing them. There's nothing."
changes.after: "I wish I could tell you. I keep looking for something in them—a mark, a colour, anything that might explain who made them or why I was wearing them. There's nothing."
changes.why: He looks down at himself six lines earlier and is already rubbing the cloth between his fingers. It's clear he's the one answering.

changes.title: Stopped, then not stopped
changes.before: There was nothing hidden in the lining. He checked every seam twice anyway, then stopped himself before beginning a third search.
changes.after: There was nothing hidden in the lining. He checked every seam twice anyway.
changes.why: He "stopped himself", yet in the next line his nail is finding another stitch when Gerolt catches his wrist. Now Gerolt is the one who stops him.

changes.title: Who says "There was someone"
changes.before: "There was someone," he managed.
changes.after: "There was someone," the boy managed.
changes.why: The sentence before it is about Gerolt, so "he" read as Gerolt speaking.

changes.title: Whose sleeve
changes.before: The boy looked down at the hand clutching his sleeve and tried to let go. His fingers did not move. Gerolt followed his gaze. Instead of pulling away, he covered the boy's hand with his own.
changes.after: The boy looked at his own hand, still clutching Gerolt's sleeve, and tried to let go. His fingers did not move. Gerolt followed his gaze. Instead of pulling away, he covered the boy's hand with his own.
changes.why: "His sleeve" read as the boy's own sleeve. It's also one fewer "looked down".
